title: Sharp cover times for random growing balls
short_statement: Develop sharp cover-time asymptotics for sequentially arriving randomly centered growing balls on compact metric spaces.
open_problem: Determine sharp cover-time laws for specified asymptotic families in the deterministic-birth model above. Separate this target from established Poisson, linear-growth results, and specify assumptions ensuring finite cover times.
background: Random coverage connects geometric probability, coupon collection, and stochastic geometry. Aldous's growing-ball model uses Poisson arrivals and constant radial growth on a compact metric space. The deterministic integer-time arrivals and general growth function in this record define a broader, different model; the cited concentration theorem does not automatically transfer. Sharp laws now exist for important Poisson Euclidean models, so the research target must distinguish arrival schedules, growth rules, and geometric classes.
full_statement: Let $(S,d)$ be a compact metric space with Borel probability measure $\mu$. At integer times $i=1,2,\ldots$, centers $X_i$ are sampled iid from $\mu$. A ball born at time $i$ has radius $r(t-i)$ at time $t\ge i$, where $r:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is deterministic, nondecreasing, and $r(0)=0$. The cover time is $$T=\inf\left\{t:S\subseteq \bigcup_{1\le i\le t} B(X_i,r(t-i))\right\}.$$ Aldous's weak-concentration theorem instead concerns Poisson birth times and linear growth; it is not a theorem for this entire deterministic-birth, arbitrary-growth model. Asymptotic questions must specify a sequence of spaces, arrival scalings, or growth scalings, and conditions ensuring finite cover times. The open problem is to determine sharp first-order constants, second-order corrections, and limiting distributions for $T$ in natural families of spaces: intervals, circles, flat tori, compact manifolds, fractals, finite metric spaces approaching a continuum, and irregular measures with nonuniform local dimension. A satisfactory answer should identify which geometric quantities, such as metric entropy, small-ball probabilities, boundary effects, and bottleneck sets, determine the cover-time law.
known_results: Aldous (2022), Section 3, equation (3.1) and Proposition 3.1, treats Poisson births of rate $\lambda$, iid centers, and radius $v(t-\tau_i)$, proving $\operatorname{Var}(C/\mathbb EC)\le c^*/\mathbb EC$, where $c^*=\sup_s\mathbb EC(s)$. This is not a result for arbitrary $r$ or deterministic birth times. Penrose and Higgs (2026), Theorems 2.2-2.3, give sharp centering and limiting laws for Poisson seeds restricted to $A\times[0,\infty)$ with linear unit growth: planar polygons and compact smoothly bounded domains in dimensions $d\ge2$. In dimension two the limit has both area and boundary contributions, not a single Gumbel term. Transferring such laws to this record's schedule requires a separate argument.

progress.summary: Sharp laws are known for related Poisson birth-growth models. No resolution of the deterministic-birth, general-growth target is inferred.

counterexample_rationale: Irregular compact spaces can refute overly simple entropy-based formulas. Finite metric examples can be checked exactly or by simulation.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search over finite metrics and growth rules can reveal candidate formulas and pathologies. Simulations can guide conjectures about constants and limiting distributions.

literature.synthesis: Aldous's concentration result and the sharp Penrose-Higgs laws concern Poisson arrivals with linear growth. They provide comparison targets and techniques, but do not establish a theorem for the deterministic schedule and arbitrary growth rule in the formal statement. Do not describe all Euclidean sharp asymptotics as missing.

reviewed.ref: David J. Aldous, 'Covering a compact space by fixed-radius or growing random balls', ALEA 19, 755-767 (2022)
reviewed.result: Section 3, Proposition 3.1: weak concentration for Poisson births and linear radial growth.
Develops sharp random covering criteria and constants in classical one-dimensional settings, showing the kind of precision missing in the general growing-ball model.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Start with intervals, circles, flat tori, and finite metric spaces. Compare uncovered-radius extremes to metric entropy integrals, and search for boundary-driven second-order terms.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A claimed asymptotic theorem must specify the class of spaces, the regularity assumptions on $\mu$, and the admissible growth functions $r$. The verifier should check that the theorem gives constants or limit laws, not merely a weak-concentration statement in a different birth-growth model. For counterexamples to proposed entropy formulas, the construction should include a sequence of compact metric probability spaces and a proof that the predicted scale differs from the true cover-time scale. Check any de-Poissonization or change-of-growth argument explicitly; specify the asymptotic parameter and finite-coverage conditions.

where_posed.text: Related Poisson, linear-growth questions occur in Aldous; the deterministic-birth, arbitrary-growth formulation here is an editorial extension, not his exact model.
